units.passage: When an AI system is used to assist in making a decision that has a material impact on institutional operations (examples include admissions screening, hiring recommendations, or financial aid analysis), the university will ensure that the use of AI is disclosed to appropriate stakeholders and that outcomes can be explained in understandable terms.
units.policy: For AI-assisted decisions with material impact on institutional operations, such as admissions screening, hiring recommendations or financial aid analysis, the university ensures AI use is disclosed to appropriate stakeholders and outcomes can be explained in understandable terms.
units.why: When AI helps make decisions with 'material impact on institutional operations (examples include admissions screening, hiring recommendations...)', 'the university will ensure that the use of AI is disclosed to appropriate stakeholders'. This tells people they are dealing with AI-assisted decisions, P103.
units.fit_note: Covers disclosure about AI-assisted institutional decisions (admissions, hiring, aid) and explainability of outcomes.

units.passage: Transparency refers to the ability to understand information about the AI system itself, as well as understanding when one is working with AI-generated (rather than human-generated) information
units.why: "understanding when one is working with AI-generated (rather than human-generated) information" describes transparency as knowing when AI is involved, nearest P103.
units.fit_note: A definition of transparency within the NIST framework summary, not a duty to tell people. / A definition of transparency in the NIST framework, not a duty.

units.passage: HR should provide employees with how and why AI is utilized in any HR processes or decision-making.
units.why: 'HR should provide employees with how and why AI is utilized in any HR processes' tells employees when AI is used on them (P103).

units.passage: If AI is used to inform decision-making, the user should outline for recipients of that decision how AI was used in the process.
units.why: When AI informs a decision, 'the user should outline for recipients of that decision how AI was used', a disclosure duty toward affected people; nearest is P103 (tell people about AI involvement).
units.fit_note: The duty is to explain AI's role in a decision, not to announce a chatbot. / Disclosure is to recipients of a university decision, not with a student submission.

units.passage: Be transparent. Individuals should be informed when AI-enabled tools are being used and/or when content has been generated with the uses of AI. Disclose when a work product was created wholly or partially using an AI tool and, if appropriate, how AI was used to create the work product.
units.why: "Individuals should be informed when AI-enabled tools are being used". The right to know when AI is involved, P103.
units.fit_note: The sentence also covers content generated with AI, which P103 does not.

units.passage: These applications are not always clear about where or when users are interacting with generative AI.
units.why: "These applications are not always clear about where or when users are interacting with generative AI" says applications do not signal AI presence. Nearest is P103, though no right to be told is declared.
units.fit_note: Notes that applications do not signal AI use; no right to know is stated.

units.passage: 2) students may not always know when they are using AI,
units.why: "students may not always know when they are using AI" is a separate premise that students cannot always tell whether a tool uses AI; nearest P103, though it concerns tool opacity.
units.fit_note: States students may not know they use AI; no right to be told is declared.

units.passage: Provide disclaimers up-front when AI will assist in decision-making.
units.why: 'Provide disclaimers up-front when AI will assist in decision-making' is a duty to tell people AI is involved, P103.

units.passage: Provide disclaimers for AI chat assistants, informing users of the potential for incorrect information and encouraging double-checking outputs.
units.why: 'disclaimers for AI chat assistants' tell users they deal with AI and its limits, so P103.
units.fit_note: Also adds a prompt to double-check outputs, which is verification advice.

units.passage: provide and seek clear information about when AI is being used and what choices are available
units.policy: provide and seek clear information about when AI is being used and what choices are available
units.why: Principle 5 also says members "should provide and seek clear information about when AI is being used", a right-to-know rule matching P103.

units.passage: UNM should inform people when AI may materially affect their learning, work, care, rights, or opportunities
units.why: UNM 'should inform people when AI may materially affect their learning, work, care, rights'; right to know about AI involvement, P103.

units.passage: Al iniciar el uso interactivo con toda IA en los sistemas de información de la Universidad, deberá indicarse efectivamente en la interfaz con el usuario esta advertencia sobre uso adecuado de la IA y responsabilidades del usuario.
units.policy: A warning about proper use of AI and user responsibilities must be effectively displayed in the interface when interactive use of any AI in University information systems begins.
units.why: When starting interactive use of any AI in University systems, a warning "deberá indicarse efectivamente en la interfaz" about proper use and user responsibilities; users are told they are dealing with AI and its rules, closest P103.
units.fit_note: The notice is about proper use and responsibilities, not specifically that the user is dealing with an AI. | Coder A: A warning about proper use and user responsibility, not a notice that the user is dealing with AI.

units.passage: The District shall promote transparency regarding institutional uses of AI that impact students, employees, or the public.
units.why: "The District shall promote transparency regarding institutional uses of AI that impact students, employees, or the public" is a duty to be open about AI use. P103 (tell people when interacting with AI) is the nearest.
units.fit_note: General transparency about institutional AI uses, not telling a person they are dealing with an AI system.

units.passage: If instructors implement a chatbot in your course, please use the following statement:
units.why: "If instructors implement a chatbot in your course, please use the following statement" tells students up front they deal with a chatbot and what it can do, P103.

units.passage: Informed Consent: When AI systems interact directly with individuals, e.g., research participants, students, faculty, or staff, informed consent is required. This includes clear communication of the purpose, scope, and potential impacts of data collection and analysis.
units.why: 'When AI systems interact directly with individuals ... informed consent is required' and the purpose, scope and impacts must be communicated. This is about telling people they deal with AI (P103) and getting consent. It conditions AI interaction on consent, so restrict; it binds whoever runs such systems, so all.
units.fit_note: Requires consent and not only notice.

units.passage: Transparency: Maintain openness about AI capabilities, limitations, and use cases. Inform users when AI is involved in decision making processes, and ensure transparency regarding its role in education, advising, and administrative tasks.
units.why: 'Inform users when AI is involved in decision making processes' is a duty to say when AI is in play: P103.

units.passage: Everyone should ensure the AI systems are transparent and explainable to professors and students, to increase trust and responsibility.
units.why: "Everyone should ensure the AI systems are transparent and explainable to professors and students"; closest to P103 (people should understand the AI they deal with).
units.fit_note: About transparency and explainability of systems, not telling people they face an AI. | Concerns explainability of AI systems to users rather than audit or monitoring.

units.passage: Inform relevant stakeholders about the use of AI in decision-making processes
units.why: "Maintain transparency: Inform relevant stakeholders about the use of AI in decision-making processes and provide opportunities for feedback and oversight"; people told when AI is used, P103.

units.passage: Notify meeting participants if AI tools are being used in your meetings
units.policy: Notify meeting participants if AI tools are being used in your meetings.
units.why: The transparency slide says to 'Notify meeting participants if AI tools are being used in your meetings'; telling people when AI is in use, P103 (P86 concerns consent to recording, this is only notification).
units.fit_note: Notice is to meeting participants about AI use in meetings, not interaction with an AI system. / Notice to meeting participants that AI tools are in use, with no consent requirement.

units.passage: Provide clear user/public notices where applicable and do not misrepresent AI as human.
units.policy: Provide clear user/public notices where applicable and do not misrepresent AI as human.
units.why: "Provide clear user/public notices where applicable and do not misrepresent AI as human" tells people when they are dealing with AI; it sits in the principle that governs all use of AI, so P103, all, general, must.

units.passage: We design, procure, and use AI systems that are explainable and strive to reduce bias. We disclose AI use to those affected by it.
units.why: Principle 5: 'We disclose AI use to those affected by it' says people should know when AI is involved (P103).
units.fit_note: Stated as institutional transparency; it does not specify student disclosure. | Covers disclosure of AI use to those affected generally, not only interaction with an AI system.

units.passage: We should protect data from disclosure and, where appropriate, obtain consent from individuals who interact with AI.
units.why: 'obtain consent from individuals who interact with AI' where appropriate; P103 is the nearest type (people's right to know they deal with AI), though consent goes beyond notice.
units.fit_note: Asks for consent from people who interact with AI, beyond telling them.

units.passage: Transparency requirements for AI decision-making processes, particularly in high-impact applications affecting student success, employment decisions, or resource allocation, will ensure that community members understand how AI systems influence decisions that affect their university experience.
units.why: 'Transparency requirements for AI decision-making processes, particularly in high-impact applications' (P103).
units.fit_note: About transparency of AI-influenced decisions rather than telling people they face an AI.
